342	  // Joined select (nostr_events + nostr_tags aliases) for tagFilters (AND semantics)
343	  JoinedSelectStatement _buildJoinedSelect(RawEventQuery query) {
344	    final base = select(nostrEvents);
345	
346	    final joins = <Join>[];
347	
348	    for (final tf in query.tagFilters!) {
349	      // Use alias to allow multiple joins on the same table
350	      final aliasTable = alias(
351	        nostrTags,
352	        'tags_${tf.tag}_${tf.value.hashCode}',
353	      );
354	
355	      joins.add(
356	        innerJoin(
357	          aliasTable,
358	          aliasTable.eventId.equalsExp(nostrEvents.id) &
359	              aliasTable.tag.equals(tf.tag) &
360	              aliasTable.value.isIn(tf.value),
361	        ),
362	      );
363	    }
364	
365	    final joined = base.join(joins);
366	
367	    _applyCommonWhereOnJoin(joined, query);
368	
369	    joined.orderBy([OrderingTerm.desc(nostrEvents.createdAt)]);
370	
371	    if (query.limit != null) {
372	      joined.limit(query.limit!);
373	    }
374	
375	    return joined;
376	  }

378	  void _applyCommonWhere(
379	    SimpleSelectStatement<NostrEvents, NostrEventData> q,
380	    RawEventQuery query,
381	  ) {
382	    if (query.ids != null && query.ids!.isNotEmpty) {
383	      q.where((e) => e.id.isIn(query.ids!));
384	    }
385	
386	    if (query.kinds != null && query.kinds!.isNotEmpty) {
387	      q.where((e) => e.kind.isIn(query.kinds!));
388	    }
389	
390	    if (query.authors != null && query.authors!.isNotEmpty) {
391	      q.where((e) => e.pubkey.isIn(query.authors!));
392	    }
393	
394	    if (query.since != null) {
395	      final sinceSec = query.since!.toUtc().millisecondsSinceEpoch ~/ 1000;
396	      q.where((e) => e.createdAt.isBiggerOrEqualValue(sinceSec));
397	    }
398	
399	    if (query.until != null) {
400	      final untilSec = query.until!.toUtc().millisecondsSinceEpoch ~/ 1000;
401	      q.where((e) => e.createdAt.isSmallerOrEqualValue(untilSec));
402	    }
403	
404	    if (query.search != null && query.search!.isNotEmpty) {
405	      final searchLower = query.search;
406	
407	      // Subquery to find event IDs with matching tag values
408	      final tagSubquery = selectOnly(nostrTags)
409	        ..addColumns([nostrTags.eventId])
410	        ..where(nostrTags.value.like('%$searchLower%'));
411	
412	      // Search in content OR in tag values
413	      q.where(
414	        (e) => e.content.like('%$searchLower%') | e.id.isInQuery(tagSubquery),
415	      );
416	    }
417	
418	    // Filter events that have at least one tag of specified type(s)
419	    if (query.hasTagTypes != null && query.hasTagTypes!.isNotEmpty) {
420	      final hasTagSubquery = selectOnly(nostrTags)
421	        ..addColumns([nostrTags.eventId])
422	        ..where(nostrTags.tag.isIn(query.hasTagTypes!));
423	
424	      q.where((e) => e.id.isInQuery(hasTagSubquery));
425	    }
426	  }

444	
445	    if (query.until != null) {

447	      joined.where(nostrEvents.createdAt.isSmallerOrEqualValue(untilSec));

449	
450	    if (query.search != null && query.search!.isNotEmpty) {
451	      final searchLower = query.search;

454	      final tagSubquery = selectOnly(nostrTags)

475	  List<NostrEvent> _mapEventRowsFromEvents(List<NostrEventData> rows) {
476	    return rows.map((row) {
477	      final decoded = jsonDecode(row.tags);
478	      final rawTags = decoded is List ? decoded : const [];
479	
480	      final tags = rawTags
481	          .cast<List>()
482	          .map((e) => e.cast<String>().toList())
483	          .toList();
484	
485	      return NostrEvent(
486	        id: row.id,
487	        kind: row.kind,
488	        pubkey: row.pubkey,
489	        createdAt: row.createdAt,
490	        content: row.content,
491	        sig: row.sig,
492	        tags: tags,
493	      );
494	    }).toList();
495	  }

510	  Future<Set<String>> filterMissingPubkeys(Set<String> pubkeys) async {
511	    if (pubkeys.isEmpty) return <String>{};
512	
513	    final pkList = pubkeys.toList();
514	
515	    // “Profile exists” == we have at least one metadata event (kind 0) for this pubkey

535	  /// Deletes events by their IDs along with their associated tags and relay info.
536	  Future<void> deleteEvents(Set<String> ids) async {
537	    if (ids.isEmpty) return;
538	
539	    final idList = ids.toList();
540	
541	    await transaction(() async {
542	      await batch((b) {
543	        //TODO: mayby double work because `onDelete: KeyAction.cascade`
544	        // Delete tags first (foreign key reference)
545	        b.deleteWhere(nostrTags, (t) => t.eventId.isIn(idList));
546	        // Delete relay info
547	        b.deleteWhere(nostrEventRelays, (r) => r.eventId.isIn(idList));
548	        // Delete the events themselves
549	        b.deleteWhere(nostrEvents, (e) => e.id.isIn(idList));
550	      });
551	    });
552	
553	    // Explicitly notify stream subscribers about table changes.
554	    // This is needed because batch operations within transactions may not
555	    // automatically trigger stream updates for joined queries.
556	    notifyUpdates({
557	      TableUpdate.onTable(nostrEvents, kind: UpdateKind.delete),
558	      TableUpdate.onTable(nostrTags, kind: UpdateKind.delete),
559	      TableUpdate.onTable(nostrEventRelays, kind: UpdateKind.delete),
560	    });
561	  }

62	  Future<Note> _execute({
63	    required String content,
64	    required String? dTag,
65	    required DateTime updatedAt,
66	    List<Label> labels = const [],
67	    Now? now,
68	    Uuid? uuid,
69	  }) async {

72	      throw const AppError.notAuthenticated();
73	    }
74	
75	    final note = Note(
76	      eventId: '',
77	      dTag: dTag ?? '',
78	      content: content,
79	      summary: '',
80	      createdAt: DateTime.fromMicrosecondsSinceEpoch(0),
81	      updatedAt: updatedAt,
82	      labels: labels,
83	    );
84	
85	    final encryptedNote = await _noteCryptoUseCase.encryptNote(
86	      note.copyWith(summary: CrerateSummaryHelper.create(note)),

97	    );

244	        ? note.dTag
245	        : (uuid ?? const Uuid()).v1();

247	    final int? initAtSeconds = initAt == null
248	        ? null
249	        : (initAt.millisecondsSinceEpoch / 1000).floor();
250	
251	    final List<List<String>> tags = [
252	      AppConfig.clientTagList(),
253	      [Tag.t.value, AppConfig.clientTagValue],
254	      [Tag.d.value, dTagValue],
255	      [Tag.p.value, pubkey],
256	      [const SummaryTag().value, note.summary],
257	      if (initAtSeconds != null) [Note.updatedAtTag, initAtSeconds.toString()],
258	      if (labels.isNotEmpty)
259	        [
260	          Note.labelsTag,
261	          ...[for (final label in labels) label.textValue],
262	        ],
263	    ];
264	
265	    final createdAt = (now ?? _now).now();
266	
267	    final event = _eventCreator.createEvent(
268	      kind: EventKind.note.value,
269	      content: note.content,
270	      createdAt: createdAt,
271	      tags: tags,
272	      pubkey: pubkey,
273	      privateKey: privateKey,
274	    );
275	
276	    // SQL-first: persist locally, then let OutboxPublisher handle relay sync
277	    // If editing an existing note (same dTag), remove old undelivered outbox entry
278	    if (note.dTag.isNotEmpty) {
279	      final previousEvents = await _eventStore.queryEvents(
280	        RawEventQuery(
281	          kinds: [EventKind.note.value],
282	          authors: [pubkey],
283	          tagFilters: [
284	            TagFilter(TagValue.d, [dTagValue]),
285	          ],
286	        ),
287	      );
288	      final oldEventIds = previousEvents
289	          .where((e) => e.id != event.id)
290	          .map((e) => e.id)
291	          .toSet();
292	      if (oldEventIds.isNotEmpty) {
293	        await _outboxDao.removeUndeliveredByEventIds(oldEventIds);
294	      }
295	    }
296	
297	    await _eventStore.upsert([event]);
298	    await _outboxDao.insert(eventId: event.id);
299	
300	    final resultNote = NoteMapper.fromNostrEvent(event);
301	
302	    if (resultNote == null) {
303	      throw const AppError.undefined();
304	    }
305	
306	    return resultNote;
307	  }

309	  @override
310	  Future<Note> deleteNote({
311	    required Note note,
312	    required String pubkey,
313	    required String privateKey,
314	    Now? now,
315	    Uuid? uuid,
316	    List<int>? randomBytes,
317	  }) async {
318	    if (note.dTag.isEmpty) {
319	      throw const AppError.common(
320	        message: 'Cannot delete a note without a dTag',
321	      );
322	    }
323	
324	    final nowTime = (now ?? _now).now();
325	    // Ensure deletion event has createdAt strictly after the original note,
326	    // so upsert replaces the old replaceable event.
327	    final createdAt = nowTime.isAfter(note.createdAt)
328	        ? nowTime
329	        : note.createdAt.add(const Duration(seconds: 1));
330	
331	    final List<List<String>> tags = [
332	      AppConfig.clientTagList(),
333	      [Tag.t.value, AppConfig.clientTagValue],
334	      [Tag.d.value, note.dTag],
335	      [Tag.p.value, pubkey],
336	    ];
337	
338	    final event = _eventCreator.createEvent(
339	      kind: EventKind.note.value,
340	      content: '',
341	      createdAt: createdAt,
342	      tags: tags,
343	      pubkey: pubkey,
344	      privateKey: privateKey,
345	    );
346	
347	    // SQL-first: persist locally, then let OutboxPublisher handle relay sync
348	    // Remove old undelivered outbox entries and old events from store
349	    final previousEvents = await _eventStore.queryEvents(
350	      RawEventQuery(
351	        kinds: [EventKind.note.value],
352	        authors: [pubkey],
353	        tagFilters: [
354	          TagFilter(TagValue.d, [note.dTag]),
355	        ],
356	      ),
357	    );
358	    final oldEventIds = previousEvents.map((e) => e.id).toSet();
359	    if (oldEventIds.isNotEmpty) {
360	      await _outboxDao.removeUndeliveredByEventIds(oldEventIds);
361	    }

The `RawEventStore` is an abstract interface with two key methods:

- `upsert(Iterable<NostrEvent> events)` → Returns `Future<void>`

### 2. Actual Implementation - watchEvents() uses Drift's watch()

**File:** `/Users/alekseypopkov/Doc/nostr_notes/nostr_notes/packages/common/lib/services/event_store/drift_event_store.dart`

The `DriftEventStore` is a thin wrapper around `NostrEventDao`.

**File:** `/Users/alekseypopkov/Doc/nostr_notes/nostr_notes/packages/common/lib/services/event_store/database/daos/nostr_event_dao.dart` (lines 302-315)

```dart
Stream<List<NostrEvent>> watchEvents(RawEventQuery query) {
  if (query.tagFilters == null || query.tagFilters!.isEmpty) {
    final selectStmt = _buildSimpleSelect(query);
    return selectStmt.watch().map(_mapEventRowsFromEvents);
  } else {
    final joined = _buildJoinedSelect(query);
    return joined.watch().map((rows) {
      final events = _deduplicateEventRowsById(
        rows.map((r) => r.readTable(nostrEvents)).toList(),
      );
      return _mapEventRowsFromEvents(events);
    });
  }
}
```

**Answer:** Yes, `watchEvents()` uses **drift's `.watch()`** method, which is a reactive stream that automatically emits whenever database changes occur. This is a continuous stream, not a one-time query.

### 3. upsert() Implementation

**File:** `/Users/alekseypopkov/Doc/nostr_notes/nostr_notes/packages/common/lib/services/event_store/database/daos/nostr_event_dao.dart` (lines 23-125)

The `upsert()` method:
1. **Filters stale replaceable events** - skips events where DB already has a newer version
2. **Handles parameterized replaceable events** (kind 30000-40000) by checking kind+pubkey+d-tag
3. **Performs batch insertions** in a transaction:
   - Deletes old versions of replaceable events
   - Inserts events with `InsertMode.insertOrReplace`
   - Deletes all tags for these events, then re-inserts new tags
   - Records relay info
4. **Handles NIP-09 deletion events** - removes events referenced by e-tags and a-tags

### 4. Note Editing Screen - Post-Save Navigation

**File:** `/Users/alekseypopkov/Doc/nostr_notes/nostr_notes/packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/edit_note_markdown_screen/edit_note_markdown_screen.dart` (lines 22-49)

```dart
case DidSaveState():
  ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar(
    SnackBar(content: Text(context.l10n.editNoteScreenSaveSuccess)),
  );

  final noteId = pathParams?.id ?? '';
  final isNew = noteId.isEmpty;

  if (isNew) {
    // NEW NOTE: Navigate to NotePreviewRoute with the dTag
    RouteHandler.of(
      context,
    )?.onRoute(NotePreviewRoute(noteId: state.note.dTag), context);
  } else {
    // EXISTING NOTE: Pop the screen
    Navigator.of(context).pop();
  }
  break;
```

**Answer:** After saving a note:
- A **success snackbar** is shown
- If it's a **new note**: navigates to `NotePreviewRoute(noteId: state.note.dTag)`
- If it's an **existing note**: pops the screen using `Navigator.of(context).pop()`

### 5. Complete Save Flow

**File:** `/Users/alekseypopkov/Doc/nostr_notes/nostr_notes/packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/edit_note_markdown_screen/bloc/markdown_edit_note_bloc.dart` (lines 77-113)

11	class GetNotesUsecase {
12	  final NotesRepository _notesRepository;
13	  final SessionUsecase _sessionUsecase;
14	  final NoteCryptoUseCase _noteCryptoUseCase;
15	
16	  GetNotesUsecase({
17	    required NotesRepository notesRepository,
18	    required SessionUsecase sessionUsecase,
19	    required NoteCryptoUseCase noteCryptoUseCase,
20	  }) : _notesRepository = notesRepository,
21	       _sessionUsecase = sessionUsecase,
22	       _noteCryptoUseCase = noteCryptoUseCase;
23	
24	  Stream<List<Note>> execute() {
25	    final keys = _sessionUsecase.currentSession.keys;
26	    final publicKey = keys?.publicKey;
27	
28	    if (publicKey == null || publicKey.isEmpty) {
29	      throw const AppError.notAuthenticated();
30	    }
31	
32	    return _notesRepository.watchNotes(pubkey: publicKey).switchMap((items) {
33	      if (items.isEmpty) {
34	        return Stream.value(<Note>[]);
35	      }
36	
37	      return Stream.fromFuture(_decryptNotes(items)).map((decryptedNotes) {
38	        return decryptedNotes.sorted(
39	          (a, b) => b.updatedAt.compareTo(a.updatedAt),
40	        );
41	      });
42	    });
43	  }
44	
45	  Future<Iterable<Note>> _decryptNotes(Iterable<Note> notes) async {
46	    final decryptedNotes = <Note>[];
47	
48	    for (final note in notes) {
49	      try {
50	        final decryptedNote = await _noteCryptoUseCase.decryptNote(note);
51	        decryptedNotes.add(decryptedNote);
52	      } catch (e, s) {
53	        log('Failed to decrypt note ${note.dTag}: $e', stackTrace: s);
54	        decryptedNotes.add(note.copyWith(error: e));
55	      }
56	    }
57	
58	    return decryptedNotes;
59	  }
60	}
61

# Plan: Fix note not appearing in list after creation

## Context

After `publishNote()` saves a note locally, it should appear in `NotesListBloc`'s list immediately via the drift watch stream chain. Instead, it often only appears after pull-to-refresh. Two cooperating bugs cause this.

Pull-to-refresh works because `_onRefreshEvent` cancels and recreates `_fetchNotesSubscription`, briefly stopping relay event upsertion. During that brief quiet, `GetNotesUsecase.execute()` can finally emit, and the recreated `_getNotesSubscription` sees the note.

---

## Root Cause 1 — `switchMap` in `GetNotesUsecase` perpetually cancels decryption

**File:** `packages/notes/lib/auth/domain/usecase/get_notes_usecase.dart:32`

\```dart
return _notesRepository.watchNotes(pubkey: publicKey).switchMap((items) {
  return Stream.fromFuture(_decryptNotes(items)).map(...);
});
\```

`FetchNotesUsecase.execute()` returns `eventsStream`, which calls `_eventStore.upsert(events)` for each relay batch buffered every 100 ms. Each upsert triggers drift's table watcher → `watchNotes` emits.

`_decryptNotes` is a sequential for-loop calling FFI crypto for every note. With many notes it takes >100 ms. With `switchMap`, each new `watchNotes` emission (every ~100 ms relay batch) cancels the current decryption and starts a fresh one. Result: `GetNotesUsecase.execute()` emits **nothing** during active relay sync. The locally-saved note's emission is silently discarded.

## Root Cause 2 — `debounceTime` prevents notes list from updating even when emissions arrive

**File:** `packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/notes_list/bloc/notes_list_bloc.dart:~123`

\```dart
_getNotesSubscription = _getNotesUsecase
    .execute()
    .debounceTime(Durations.medium2)   // 300 ms silence required
    .listen(...)
\```

`debounceTime(300ms)` waits for 300 ms of silence from `GetNotesUsecase`. During relay sync, even if decryption occasionally completes and emits, the next relay batch (≤100 ms later) resets the timer. The listener never fires.

---

## Secondary Bug — OutboxPublisher tight retry loop

**File:** `packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart:248-259`

\```dart
Future<void> _handleFailure(OutboxEventData item, String reason) async {
  await _outboxDao.retryFailed(item.eventId);   // ← immediately back to 'pending'
  _retryTimer?.cancel();
  _retryTimer = Timer(_retryDelay, _processQueue);
}
\```

`retryFailed` resets status to `pending` immediately. This triggers `watchUndelivered` → `_onPendingEvents` sets `_refreshRequested = true`. The do-while loop in `_processQueue` sees `_refreshRequested = true` and loops immediately, retrying the same event before the 20-second timer fires. Creates a tight retry loop that burns CPU and hits relay rate limits when a relay is unavailable.

---

## Fixes

### Fix 1 — Add debounce before `switchMap` in `GetNotesUsecase`

`packages/notes/lib/auth/domain/usecase/get_notes_usecase.dart`

\```dart
// Before (line 32):
return _notesRepository.watchNotes(pubkey: publicKey).switchMap((items) {

// After:
return _notesRepository.watchNotes(pubkey: publicKey)
    .debounceTime(const Duration(milliseconds: 100))
    .switchMap((items) {
\```

Batches rapid `watchNotes` emissions. Decryption starts only after a 100 ms quiet period, so relay batches (arriving every ~100 ms) don't perpetually cancel it. On note creation (single emission with no relay burst), decryption starts within 100 ms.

### Fix 2 — Replace `debounceTime` with `throttleTime(trailing: true)` in `NotesListBloc`

`packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/notes_list/bloc/notes_list_bloc.dart`

\```dart
// Before (~line 123):
.debounceTime(Durations.medium2)

// After:
.throttleTime(Durations.medium2, trailing: true)
\```

`throttleTime` with `trailing: true` guarantees the listener fires at least once per 300 ms window using the latest emission, even during continuous relay sync. Unlike `debounceTime`, it does not require silence — it fires the trailing edge of every window.

### Fix 3 — Fix OutboxPublisher tight retry loop

`packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart`

\```dart
// Before:
Future<void> _handleFailure(OutboxEventData item, String reason) async {
  ...
  await _outboxDao.retryFailed(item.eventId);
  _retryTimer?.cancel();
  _retryTimer = Timer(_retryDelay, _processQueue);
}

// After:
Future<void> _handleFailure(OutboxEventData item, String reason) async {
  ...
  await _outboxDao.markFailed(item.eventId, reason);   // keep as 'failed' — won't re-enter getPending()
  _retryTimer?.cancel();
  _retryTimer = Timer(_retryDelay, () async {
    await _outboxDao.retryFailed(item.eventId);        // reset to 'pending' only after delay
    _processQueue();
  });
}
\```

Event stays in `failed` status immediately after failure → `getPending()` won't pick it up → no tight loop. After 20 s, the timer resets it to `pending` and triggers processing.

---

## Files to modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/notes/lib/auth/domain/usecase/get_notes_usecase.dart` | Add `.debounceTime(const Duration(milliseconds: 100))` before `.switchMap` |
| `packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/notes_list/bloc/notes_list_bloc.dart` | Replace `.debounceTime(Durations.medium2)` with `.throttleTime(Durations.medium2, trailing: true)` |
| `packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart` | In `_handleFailure`: `markFailed` + retry-after-delay instead of immediate `retryFailed` |

---

## Verification

\```bash
cd packages/notes && fvm flutter test
\```

Manual test:
1. Open app while relay is actively syncing (visible in debug logs as rapid upsert calls)
2. Create a new note — verify it appears in the list within ~400 ms **without** pull-to-refresh
3. Disconnect relay, create a note — verify OutboxPublisher logs show one attempt, then a 20 s pause before retry (not a tight loop)

7	Pull-to-refresh works because `_onRefreshEvent` cancels and recreates `_fetchNotesSubscription`, briefly stopping relay event upsertion. During that brief quiet, `GetNotesUsecase.execute()` can finally emit, and the recreated `_getNotesSubscription` sees the note.

11	## Root Cause 1 — `switchMap` in `GetNotesUsecase` perpetually cancels decryption
12	
13	**File:** `packages/notes/lib/auth/domain/usecase/get_notes_usecase.dart:32`
14	
15	```dart
16	return _notesRepository.watchNotes(pubkey: publicKey).switchMap((items) {
17	  return Stream.fromFuture(_decryptNotes(items)).map(...);
18	});
19	```
20	
21	`FetchNotesUsecase.execute()` returns `eventsStream`, which calls `_eventStore.upsert(events)` for each relay batch buffered every 100 ms. Each upsert triggers drift's table watcher → `watchNotes` emits.
22	
23	`_decryptNotes` is a sequential for-loop calling FFI crypto for every note. With many notes it takes >100 ms. With `switchMap`, each new `watchNotes` emission (every ~100 ms relay batch) cancels the current decryption and starts a fresh one. Result: `GetNotesUsecase.execute()` emits **nothing** during active relay sync. The locally-saved note's emission is silently discarded.
24	
25	## Root Cause 2 — `debounceTime` prevents notes list from updating even when emissions arrive
26	
27	**File:** `packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/notes_list/bloc/notes_list_bloc.dart:~123`
28	
29	```dart
30	_getNotesSubscription = _getNotesUsecase
31	    .execute()
32	    .debounceTime(Durations.medium2)   // 300 ms silence required
33	    .listen(...)
34	```
35	
36	`debounceTime(300ms)` waits for 300 ms of silence from `GetNotesUsecase`. During relay sync, even if decryption occasionally completes and emits, the next relay batch (≤100 ms later) resets the timer. The listener never fires.

41	
42	**File:** `packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart:248-259`
43	
44	```dart
45	Future<void> _handleFailure(OutboxEventData item, String reason) async {
46	  await _outboxDao.retryFailed(item.eventId);   // ← immediately back to 'pending'
47	  _retryTimer?.cancel();
48	  _retryTimer = Timer(_retryDelay, _processQueue);
49	}
50	```
51	
52	`retryFailed` resets status to `pending` immediately. This triggers `watchUndelivered` → `_onPendingEvents` sets `_refreshRequested = true`. The do-while loop in `_processQueue` sees `_refreshRequested = true` and loops immediately, retrying the same event before the 20-second timer fires. Creates a tight retry loop that burns CPU and hits relay rate limits when a relay is unavailable.

---

## Root causes

**Root Cause 1 — `switchMap` cancels decryption on every relay batch**

`GetNotesUsecase.execute()` ([get_notes_usecase.dart:32](packages/notes/lib/auth/domain/usecase/get_notes_usecase.dart#L32)):
```dart
return _notesRepository.watchNotes(pubkey: publicKey).switchMap((items) {
  return Stream.fromFuture(_decryptNotes(items)).map(...);
});
```
`eventsStream` batches relay events every 100 ms and upserts them → drift fires `watchNotes` every ~100 ms. `_decryptNotes` is a sequential FFI for-loop that takes >100 ms for many notes. With `switchMap`, each new `watchNotes` emission *cancels the previous decryption* and starts fresh. During active relay sync, `GetNotesUsecase.execute()` emits nothing. The locally-saved note's emission is silently discarded.

**Root Cause 2 — `debounceTime` blocks updates even on the rare emission that makes it through**

`NotesListBloc._setupSubscription()` ([notes_list_bloc.dart:122](packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/notes_list/bloc/notes_list_bloc.dart#L122)):
```dart
_getNotesUsecase.execute().debounceTime(Durations.medium2).listen(...)
```
`debounceTime(300ms)` requires 300 ms of silence. Relay batches arrive every ~100 ms, constantly resetting the timer. The listener never fires.

**Secondary bug — `OutboxPublisher` tight retry loop**

`_handleFailure` ([outbox_publisher.dart:255](packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart#L255)):
```dart
await _outboxDao.retryFailed(item.eventId);  // immediately resets to 'pending'
_retryTimer?.cancel();
_retryTimer = Timer(_retryDelay, _processQueue);  // 20s timer, but bypassed
```
`retryFailed` puts the event back to `pending` immediately → `watchUndelivered` emits → `_refreshRequested = true` → the do-while loop in `_processQueue` retries immediately, bypassing the 20-second timer.

---

## Proposed fixes

**Fix 1** — [get_notes_usecase.dart:32](packages/notes/lib/auth/domain/usecase/get_notes_usecase.dart#L32): `switchMap` → `exhaustMap`

`exhaustMap` ignores incoming `watchNotes` emissions while decryption is running (instead of cancelling it). Decryption always completes → stream emits → new note appears. Between decryption cycles, the next relay batch triggers a new decryption with the latest state.

**Fix 2** — [notes_list_bloc.dart:122](packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/notes_list/bloc/notes_list_bloc.dart#L122): `.debounceTime(Durations.medium2)` → `.throttleTime(Durations.medium2, trailing: true)`

`throttleTime(trailing: true)` guarantees the listener fires at least once per 300 ms window even during continuous relay sync. Preserves the original intent (rate-limit UI rebuilds) without blocking forever.

**Fix 3** — [outbox_publisher.dart:255](packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart#L255): immediate `markFailed` + delayed `retryAllFailed`

```dart
await _outboxDao.markFailed(item.eventId, reason);  // stays 'failed' — getPending() ignores it
_retryTimer?.cancel();
_retryTimer = Timer(_retryDelay, () async {
  await _outboxDao.retryAllFailed();  // resets ALL failed events after 20s
  _processQueue();
});
```
`getPending()` only returns `pending`-status events, so the do-while loop exits cleanly. `retryAllFailed` (already in `OutboxDaoInterface`) handles the multiple-failure case where earlier per-item timers were cancelled.

| [outbox_publisher.dart:255](packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart#L255) | `retryFailed` → `markFailed` + delayed `retryAllFailed` |

The key difference is that `refresh()` is a deliberate external trigger, whereas the tight loop is just repeatedly checking the same failed events. So if the relay becomes available between when the loop exits and when `refresh()` is called, the note finally publishes—making `refresh()` causal rather than coincidental. resource limit. Each retry attempt spawns a new `NostrClient` with a fresh WebSocket connection, and if the retry loop is firing every few milliseconds, it's creating and destroying connections so rapidly that the relay might be rate-limiting or rejecting all subsequent attempts. When the user manually refreshes, `_outbox.refresh()` is called, but `_isProcessing` might still be true from the ongoing loop, so the refresh just sets `_refreshRequested = true` without actually doing anything. The real issue is that the tight retry loop bypasses the 20-second timer entirely, causing this cascade of failed connections and rate limiting that blocks even new notes from being published. I'm seeing that when a failure occurs through the non-exception path (when the relay report shows no success), `_handleFailure` is called but there's no rethrow, so the loop just continues normally to the next item. In the exception path, the rethrow propagates up to `_processQueue`'s error handler, which also logs and continues the loop. Either way, the queue keeps processing subsequent items after a failure. Reviewing the full structure of `_publishEvent` to understand the control flow — the outer catch block handles exceptions, while the non-exception failure path (when `!report.isAnySuccess`) goes through `_handleFailure` without rethrowing, allowing the loop to continue to the next event. block continues to fire asynchronously after the loop exits, which means the do-while condition checks `_refreshRequested` before the stream has a chance to set it to true, causing the loop to exit prematurely instead of triggering the retry cycle.

The actual retry loop happens between successive `_processQueue` calls: after the first call completes and `_isProcessing` is set to false, the deferred stream callback fires and invokes `_processQueue` again with the failed events. Each cycle involves async database writes and WebSocket operations, so the timing depends on how quickly the relay responds—if it's unavailable, the cycle might complete in seconds rather than minutes.

I think I've been overcomplicating this. The key findings are: the lifecycle handling in main.dart appears sound, the tight retry loop is genuinely a bug that can trigger relay rate limiting and block new note publishing when the relay is temporarily unavailable, and the proposed fix using `markFailed` with delayed retry is the right solution. I should verify whether the note creation's `watchUndelivered` emission properly triggers `_processQueue` in edge cases, though the code structure suggests it should.

The most likely explanation for notes not being published is a transient relay outage triggering the tight retry loop, which then gets rate-limited before the relay recovers—and Fix 3 solves this by introducing proper delays between retry attempts. There's also the possibility that a slow relay connection (not completely down) causes the publisher's timeout to fire, initiating the same problematic retry cycle.

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Plan: Fix note not appearing in list after creation

## Context

After `publishNote()` saves a note locally, it should appear in `NotesListBloc`'s list immediately via the drift watch stream chain. Instead, it often only appears after pull-to-refresh. Two cooperating bugs cause this.

Pull-to-refresh works because `_onRefreshEvent` cancels and recreates `_fetchNotesSubscription`, briefly stopping relay event upsertion. During that brief quiet, `GetNotesUsecase.execute()` can finally emit, and the recreated `_getNotesSubscription` sees the note.

---

## Root Cause 1 — `switchMap` in `GetNotesUsecase` perpetually cancels decryption

**File:** `packages/notes/lib/auth/domain/usecase/get_notes_usecase.dart:32`

```dart
return _notesRepository.watchNotes(pubkey: publicKey).switchMap((items) {
  return Stream.fromFuture(_decryptNotes(items)).map(...);
});
```

`FetchNotesUsecase.execute()` returns `eventsStream`, which calls `_eventStore.upsert(events)` for each relay batch buffered every 100 ms. Each upsert triggers drift's table watcher → `watchNotes` emits.

`_decryptNotes` is a sequential for-loop calling FFI crypto for every note. With many notes it takes >100 ms. With `switchMap`, each new `watchNotes` emission (every ~100 ms relay batch) cancels the current decryption and starts a fresh one. Result: `GetNotesUsecase.execute()` emits **nothing** during active relay sync. The locally-saved note's emission is silently discarded.

## Root Cause 2 — `debounceTime` prevents notes list from updating even when emissions arrive

**File:** `packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/notes_list/bloc/notes_list_bloc.dart:~123`

```dart
_getNotesSubscription = _getNotesUsecase
    .execute()
    .debounceTime(Durations.medium2)   // 300 ms silence required
    .listen(...)
```

`debounceTime(300ms)` waits for 300 ms of silence from `GetNotesUsecase`. During relay sync, even if decryption occasionally completes and emits, the next relay batch (≤100 ms later) resets the timer. The listener never fires.

---

## Secondary Bug — OutboxPublisher tight retry loop

**File:** `packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart:248-259`

```dart
Future<void> _handleFailure(OutboxEventData item, String reason) async {
  await _outboxDao.retryFailed(item.eventId);   // ← immediately back to 'pending'
  _retryTimer?.cancel();
  _retryTimer = Timer(_retryDelay, _processQueue);
}
```

`retryFailed` resets status to `pending` immediately. This triggers `watchUndelivered` → `_onPendingEvents` sets `_refreshRequested = true`. The do-while loop in `_processQueue` sees `_refreshRequested = true` and loops immediately, retrying the same event before the 20-second timer fires. Creates a tight retry loop that burns CPU and hits relay rate limits when a relay is unavailable.

---

## Fixes

### Fix 1 — Replace `switchMap` with `exhaustMap` in `GetNotesUsecase`

`packages/notes/lib/auth/domain/usecase/get_notes_usecase.dart:32`

```dart
// Before:
return _notesRepository.watchNotes(pubkey: publicKey).switchMap((items) {

// After:
return _notesRepository.watchNotes(pubkey: publicKey).exhaustMap((items) {
```

`exhaustMap` ignores new `watchNotes` emissions while decryption is in flight, rather than cancelling it:
- `watchNotes` emits (note just saved) → decryption starts immediately
- Relay batches arrive every ~100 ms → **ignored** by `exhaustMap` during decryption
- Decryption completes (~200 ms for many notes via FFI) → stream emits with the new note ✅
- Next relay batch emission → fresh decryption starts with latest state

This allows the list to update every `~decryptionTime` ms during relay sync. Unlike `debounceTime + switchMap`, it never blocks updates — as long as any emission arrives between decryption cycles, it proceeds.

`exhaustMap` is available from `package:rxdart/rxdart.dart` which is already imported.

### Fix 2 — Replace `debounceTime` with `throttleTime(trailing: true)` in `NotesListBloc`

`packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/notes_list/bloc/notes_list_bloc.dart:122`

```dart
// Before:
.debounceTime(Durations.medium2)

// After:
.throttleTime(Durations.medium2, trailing: true)
```

`throttleTime` with `trailing: true` fires at least once per 300 ms window using the latest emission, even during continuous relay sync. Unlike `debounceTime`, it does not require silence — it fires the trailing edge of every window. Preserves the original intent (rate-limit UI rebuilds) without blocking updates indefinitely.

### Fix 3 — Fix OutboxPublisher tight retry loop with tiered retry delay

`packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart:248-258`

```dart
// Before:
Future<void> _handleFailure(OutboxEventData item, String reason) async {
  ...
  await _outboxDao.retryFailed(item.eventId);
  _retryTimer?.cancel();
  _retryTimer = Timer(_retryDelay, _processQueue);
}

// After:
Future<void> _handleFailure(OutboxEventData item, String reason) async {
  ...
  await _outboxDao.markFailed(item.eventId, reason);
  _retryTimer?.cancel();

  final ageMs = DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch - item.createdAt;
  final delay = ageMs < 5000 ? const Duration(seconds: 3) : _retryDelay;

  _retryTimer = Timer(delay, () async {
    await _outboxDao.retryAllFailed();
    _processQueue();
  });
}
```

`markFailed` sets status to `failed` immediately → `getPending()` (filters to `pending` only) won't pick it up → do-while exits → no tight loop. `watchUndelivered` still emits (it includes `failed`) but the next `getPending()` call returns nothing.

Tiered delay:
- **Fresh event** (outbox entry < 5 s old): retries after 3 s — covers transient relay hiccups without hammering.
- **Old event**: retries after 20 s (`_retryDelay`) — avoids rate-limiting during prolonged relay unavailability.

After the timer fires, `retryAllFailed()` resets ALL failed events to `pending` (handles multiple-failure case where earlier timers were cancelled by later failures) and `_processQueue()` picks them all up. Both `markFailed` and `retryAllFailed` exist in `OutboxDaoInterface`.

---

## Files to modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/notes/lib/auth/domain/usecase/get_notes_usecase.dart:32` | `switchMap` → `exhaustMap` |
| `packages/notes/lib/auth/presentation/notes_list/bloc/notes_list_bloc.dart:122` | `.debounceTime(Durations.medium2)` → `.throttleTime(Durations.medium2, trailing: true)` |
| `packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart:255` | `retryFailed(item.eventId)` → `markFailed(item.eventId, reason)` + delayed `retryAllFailed()` |

---

## Verification

cd packages/notes && fvm flutter test
```

1. Open app while relay is actively syncing (visible in debug logs as rapid upsert calls)
2. Create a new note — verify it appears in the list within ~400 ms **without** pull-to-refresh
3. Disconnect relay, create a note — verify OutboxPublisher logs show one attempt, then a 20 s pause before retry (not a tight loop)
```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-14 10:19:52Z)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user is asking about the difference between `switchMap` and `exhaustMap` in the context of the code they're looking at. They've selected `exhaustMap` on line 32 of `get_notes_usecase.dart`.

Let me explain the difference clearly and concisely in the context of this specific code.

`switchMap`: when a new event arrives, cancels the current inner stream/future and starts a new one.
`exhaustMap`: when a new event arrives while an inner stream/future is in progress, ignores it. Only processes the next event after the current one completes.

In the context of `watchNotes().exhaustMap((items) => Stream.fromFuture(_decryptNotes(items)))`:
With `switchMap`, each new batch from the relay would immediately cancel the ongoing decryption and start fresh—so if batches arrive every 100ms but decryption takes 200ms, it never completes. With `exhaustMap`, new emissions are dropped while decryption is running, and only after the current decryption finishes does the next batch get processed. This means the notes list stays consistent without interruptions.
</details></think>

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-14 10:19:59Z)**_

Оба оператора разворачивают каждый элемент внешнего стрима во внутренний стрим. Разница — что делать, когда внешний эмитит новый элемент пока внутренний ещё работает:

| | Новый элемент пришёл пока идёт `_decryptNotes` |
|---|---|
| `switchMap` | Отменяет текущее, запускает новое |
| `exhaustMap` | Игнорирует новый элемент |

**В данном контексте:**

Relay батч каждые ~100 мс → `watchNotes` эмитит → `_decryptNotes` (FFI-цикл по всем заметкам, ~200+ мс):

```
switchMap:
  t=0ms   watchNotes → старт _decryptNotes
  t=100ms watchNotes → ОТМЕНА, старт заново
  t=200ms watchNotes → ОТМЕНА, старт заново
  → никогда не доходит до emit

exhaustMap:
  t=0ms   watchNotes → старт _decryptNotes
  t=100ms watchNotes → проигнорирован (идёт decrypt)
  t=200ms watchNotes → проигнорирован (идёт decrypt)
  t=210ms _decryptNotes завершился → emit ✅
  t=300ms watchNotes → старт нового _decryptNotes (актуальные данные)
```

**Трейдофф** `exhaustMap`: список обновляется с данными на момент начала текущего `_decryptNotes`, без учёта relay-событий, пришедших за время дешифровки (~200 мс). Но следующий relay-батч сразу запустит новую дешифровку — итоговое отставание не более `decryptionTime`.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The factory shows that ads are only used on iOS, and for Android (and all other platforms), `AdsServiceStub` is returned. So AdMob is NOT used on Android. But `google_mobile_ads` is listed as a dependency and its `MobileAdsInitProvider` is auto-registered as a ContentProvider in Android via the plugin registration - that's why it crashes even though we don't use ads on Android.

The fix options:
1. Add a fake AdMob App ID to AndroidManifest.xml (test ID: `ca-app-pub-3940256099942544~3347511913`)
2. Disable the `MobileAdsInitProvider` in AndroidManifest.xml using `tools:node="remove"` to prevent the AdMob SDK from initializing on Android. Since we're not actually using ads on Android, this is the cleaner approach. The standard production approach would be to add metadata with a real AdMob App ID, but disabling the provider entirely is simpler for our case.

Actually, the simplest solution is to add Google's official test App ID for Android in the manifest metadata. This prevents the crash without requiring a real AdMob ID, and since the Android implementation uses `AdsServiceStub` anyway, a test ID is harmless. The user can replace it with their real AdMob App ID later if they decide to enable ads on Android.
</details></think>

import 'package:common/domain/error/app_error.dart';
import 'package:common/domain/error/error_messages_provider.dart';
import 'package:nostr/model/user_keys.dart';

abstract class KeyToolRepository {
  UserKeys getUserKeysWithNsec({required String? nsec});
  UserKeys getUserKeysWithPrivateKey({required String? privateKey});
  String createSig({required String rawMessage, required String privateKey});
  String generateNsecKey();
}

abstract class KeysError extends AppError {
  const KeysError({required super.reason});
}

final class EmptyNsecError extends KeysError {
  const EmptyNsecError() : super(reason: 'Nsec cannot be empty');

  @override
  String get message => ErrorMessagesProvider.defaultProvider.emptyNsec;
}

final class InvalidNsecError extends KeysError {
  const InvalidNsecError() : super(reason: 'Invalid NSEC key format');

  @override
  String get message => ErrorMessagesProvider.defaultProvider.invalidNsecFormat;
}

final class InvalidPrivateKeyError extends KeysError {
  const InvalidPrivateKeyError() : super(reason: 'Invalid private key');

  @override
  String get message => ErrorMessagesProvider.defaultProvider.emptyPubkey;
}

final class EmptyPubkeyError extends KeysError {
  const EmptyPubkeyError() : super(reason: 'Public key cannot be empty');

  @override
  String get message => ErrorMessagesProvider.defaultProvider.emptyPubkey;
}

```dart
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
import 'package:nostr/key_tool/key_tool.dart';
import 'package:nostr_notes/l10n/localization.dart';

mixin NsecValidator {
  String? validateNsec(BuildContext context, String? value) {
    final l10n = context.l10n;
    if (value == null || value.trim().isEmpty) {
      return l10n.onboardingNsecPageValidationEmpty;
    }
    final trimmed = value.trim();
    if (trimmed.startsWith('npub')) {
      return l10n.onboardingNsecPageValidationNpub;
    }
    final privateKey = KeyTool.tryDecodeNsecKeyToPrivateKey(trimmed);
    if (privateKey == null) {
      return l10n.onboardingNsecPageValidationInvalid;
    }
    return null;
  }
}

```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user is asking if there's something like `ensureVisible` to make sure the button is visible when the keyboard appears. 

In Flutter, there are several approaches to ensure a widget is visible when the keyboard appears:

1. `Scrollable.ensureVisible(context)` - scrolls the nearest `Scrollable` to make the context's widget visible
2. Using a `ScrollController` and calling `animateTo` when keyboard appears
3. Using `SingleChildScrollView` with proper padding (which we already did)

The approach already implemented (`SingleChildScrollView` with `viewInsetsOf` padding) should work - it gives the scroll view enough space to scroll to show content above the keyboard. 

The issue is that the scroll view doesn't automatically scroll to the button when the keyboard appears. I could leverage the existing `didChangeMetrics` listener to actively scroll to the button using `Scrollable.ensureVisible` with a `GlobalKey` attached to the button, ensuring it comes into view when the keyboard shows up. both approaches together makes sense — the padding gives the scroll view enough room, and `ensureVisible` automatically scrolls to show the button when the keyboard appears.
</details></think>

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-14 12:42:28Z)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user is asking why I used `SingleChildScrollView + Column` instead of just `ListView`. Good question. Let me think about this...

In this specific case:
- The content is inside a dialog (`AppAlertDialog` → `AlertDialog`)
- `AlertDialog`'s `content` expects a fixed-height widget. `AlertDialog` wraps the content in a `Flexible` which works with `SingleChildScrollView` because SCW has a known content size.
- `ListView` is lazy and has infinite scroll direction extent by default — it works fine in most contexts, but inside an `AlertDialog.content`, it would need to be constrained (e.g., with `shrinkWrap: true`)
- With `SingleChildScrollView + Column` using `mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min`, the column naturally sizes to its content and scrolling only activates when needed, making it the cleaner choice for a dialog that needs to scroll when the keyboard appears. `ListView` would work too but requires `shrinkWrap: true` and is really designed for lazy-rendering long lists.
</details></think>

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-14 12:42:30Z)**_

В диалоге `AlertDialog` обёртывает `content` во `Flexible` без явных ограничений по высоте. `ListView` в этом контексте бросает ошибку unbounded constraints, если не добавить `shrinkWrap: true`.

`SingleChildScrollView + Column(mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min)` — стандартный паттерн для диалогов: колонна сжимается до содержимого, прокрутка включается только когда содержимое не влезает. `ListView(shrinkWrap: true)` тоже сработал бы, но `shrinkWrap` дороже и семантически лишний — здесь не список динамических элементов.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-14 12:56:10Z)**_

Диагноз подтверждён. Вот что происходит:

**Заметка застряла в статусе `broadcasting`.**

Последовательность:
1. `_publishEvent` вызывает `markBroadcasting` → статус `broadcasting`, затем `await publisher.execute()`.
2. Приложение уходит в фон (отсюда поток `paused` в логах) → iOS замораживает процесс. Сетевой `await` **никогда не завершается**, поэтому ни `markSent`, ни `_handleFailure` не вызываются. Статус остаётся `broadcasting`.
3. При перезапуске/resume: `_processQueue` → `getPending()` возвращает **только** `pending` ([outbox_dao.dart:29-34](packages/common/lib/services/event_store/database/daos/outbox_dao.dart#L29-L34)). Orphan в `broadcasting` ей не виден → ни одного лога публикации.
4. Но `watchUndelivered()` включает `broadcasting` ([outbox_dao.dart:47-58](packages/common/lib/services/event_store/database/daos/outbox_dao.dart#L47-L58)) → часики горят.
5. 20-секундный таймер не выставлялся (мы не дошли до `_handleFailure`), а `retryAllFailed()` сбрасывает только `failed` → `broadcasting` он никогда не реанимирует.

Итог: заметка осиротела в `broadcasting` навсегда — без логов и без ретраев. Именно это ты и видишь.

**Фикс:** при старте/возобновлении реанимировать «зависшие» `broadcasting`-события обратно в `pending`. Добавлю метод в DAO и вызову его в `init()` и `resume()`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-14 16:54:48Z)**_

All 22 tests pass. Готово.

## Что было не так

Причина оказалась **не в `_handleFailure`** (туда и правда не заходило). Заметка застревала в статусе **`broadcasting`**:

1. `_publishEvent` → `markBroadcasting` (статус `broadcasting`) → `await publisher.execute()`.
2. Приложение уходит в фон (поток `paused` в логах) → iOS замораживает процесс. Сетевой `await` не завершается — ни `markSent`, ни `_handleFailure` не вызываются. Статус навсегда остаётся `broadcasting`.
3. `getPending()` берёт **только** `pending` → orphan ей невидим → нет логов публикации/ошибки/ретрая.
4. `watchUndelivered()` включает `broadcasting` → часики горят.
5. `retryAllFailed()` сбрасывает только `failed` → реанимировать orphan было нечем.

## Фикс

- [outbox_dao.dart](packages/common/lib/services/event_store/database/daos/outbox_dao.dart) + интерфейс: новый `resetStaleBroadcasting({olderThan})` — возвращает зависшие `broadcasting` → `pending` (с порогом по `lastAttemptAt`, чтобы не трогать реально летящую публикацию).
- [outbox_publisher.dart](packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart):
  - `init()` — сбрасывает `_isProcessing` и реанимирует **все** `broadcasting` (на старте нет летящих публикаций).
  - `resume()` — реанимирует `broadcasting` старше 30с, затем дренит очередь.
- Тесты: обновил 2 устаревших (они проверяли старый `retryFailed` вместо `markFailed`+таймер) и добавил 2 на `resetStaleBroadcasting`.

Теперь при следующем запуске/возврате из фона застрявшая «Bugs» вернётся в `pending` и реально уйдёт на реле.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-14 17:02:01Z)**_

Проанализировал все использования. Вот что выяснилось.

## Что статусы и поля делают на самом деле

Единственный внешний потребитель outbox — [get_pending_usecase_impl.dart](packages/notes/lib/auth/data/get_pending_usecase_impl.dart#L12): он сводит `watchUndelivered()` к `Set<String>` ID. Ему нужно только «какие события ещё не доставлены» (часики). Статусы, `confirmedRelays`, `attemptCount`, `failureReason` он не читает.

| Элемент | Задумка | Реальность |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | надо отправить | нужен |
| `broadcasting` | «сейчас летит» | **источник твоего бага** с orphan; дублирует in-memory `_isProcessing` |
| `sent` | доставлено | используется только чтобы исключить из выборок. `cleanup`/`deleteSent` **в проде не вызываются** → строки `sent` копятся вечно (утечка) |
| `failed` | была ошибка | нужен лишь чтобы `getPending` пропускал событие до ретрая по таймеру |
| `confirmedRelays` | какие реле подтвердили | **нигде не читается** |
| `failureReason` | дебаг | **нигде не читается**, только inline-лог |
| `attemptCount` | бэкофф | инкрементит только `retryFailed` (мёртв); задержка ретрая считается по `createdAt`, а не по нему |
| `getFailed`, `retryFailed`, `cleanupOldSent`, `deleteSent` | — | в проде **не вызываются** (только тесты/интерфейс) |

## Вывод: модель сводится к «строка есть ⇒ не доставлено»

Твоя интуиция верна по всем трём пунктам. Outbox-у достаточно **нуля статусов**:

- **success → удалить строку** (вместо `markSent`+`sent`). Заодно чинит утечку `sent`.
- **failure → ничего не писать**, оставить строку; ретраит таймер publisher-а. (Важно: отсутствие записи в БД = нет лишней эмиссии `watchUndelivered` = нет тайт-лупа, ради которого вводился `failed`.)
- **конкурентность** в рамках сессии уже держит in-memory `_isProcessing` — `broadcasting` для этого не нужен.

Таблица превращается в `{eventId, createdAt}`. Удаляются ~8 методов и 4 колонки.

Главный бонус: **твой баг с «Bugs» чинится в корне** — нет состояния `broadcasting`, в котором можно застрять. Строка просто живёт, пока её не удалят по факту успеха. Мой патч `resetStaleBroadcasting` тогда не нужен — он был костылём вокруг лишней концепции.

**Цена:** при падении прямо во время отправки возможна повторная отправка на реле — безвредно (реле дедуплицируют по id, а 30023 вообще replaceable). И теряется персистентный `failureReason` (остаётся лог).

## Один реальный развилочный вопрос — глубина

Это единственное, что влияет на объём и затрагивает уже установленные у пользователей БД.

218	          name: 'OutboxPublisher',

222	
223	      final event = events.first;
224	      final relays = _relaysListRepo.getRelaysList();
225	
226	      if (relays.isEmpty) {
227	        await _outboxDao.markFailed(item.eventId, 'No relays configured');
228	        dev.log(

230	          name: 'OutboxPublisher',

232	        return;
233	      }
234	
235	      final client = NostrClient(channelFactory: _channelFactory);
236	      try {
237	        client.addRelays(relays);
238	
239	        final publisher = NostrPublisher(client: client, event: event);
240	        final report = await publisher.execute();
241	
242	        if (!report.isAnySuccess) {

246	              .where((e) => e.isOk)

259	      } finally {

import 'dart:async';
import 'dart:developer' as dev;

import 'package:connectivity_plus/connectivity_plus.dart';
import 'package:nostr/nostr_client/channel_factory.dart';
import 'package:nostr/nostr_client/nostr_client.dart';
import 'package:nostr/nostr_client/nostr_publisher.dart';
import 'package:common/domain/repo/relays_list_repo.dart';
import 'package:nostr_notes/core/event_kind.dart';
import 'package:common/tools/disposable.dart';
import 'package:common/services/event_store/database/app_database.dart';
import 'package:common/services/event_store/database/daos/outbox_dao_interface.dart';
import 'package:common/services/event_store/raw_event_store.dart';
import 'package:rxdart/rxdart.dart';

/// Watches the outbox table and publishes its events to Nostr relays.
///
/// This is the "Nostr Adapter" layer that handles outbound sync from SQL to
/// relays. The app core writes to SQL + outbox, and this service publishes in
/// the background.
///
/// The outbox is a plain queue: **a row exists iff the event still needs to
/// reach relays.** On success the row is deleted; on failure it is left in
/// place and retried later. Concurrency within a session is serialized by
/// [_isProcessing], so no per-row "in flight" state is needed.
class OutboxPublisher implements Disposable {
  OutboxPublisher({
    required OutboxDaoInterface outboxDao,
    required RawEventStore rawEventStore,
    required RelaysListRepo relaysListRepo,
    required ChannelFactory channelFactory,
    required Connectivity connectivity,
    this.connectivityDebounce = const Duration(seconds: 2),
  }) : _outboxDao = outboxDao,
       _rawEventStore = rawEventStore,
       _relaysListRepo = relaysListRepo,
       _channelFactory = channelFactory,
       _connectivity = connectivity;

  final OutboxDaoInterface _outboxDao;
  final RawEventStore _rawEventStore;
  final RelaysListRepo _relaysListRepo;
  final ChannelFactory _channelFactory;
  final Connectivity _connectivity;
  final Duration connectivityDebounce;

  StreamSubscription<List<OutboxEventData>>? _subscription;
  StreamSubscription<List<ConnectivityResult>>? _connectivitySubscription;
  Timer? _retryTimer;
  bool _isProcessing = false;
  bool _isPaused = false;
  bool _isDisposing = false;
  bool _refreshRequested = false;

  static const _retryDelay = Duration(seconds: 20);

  Future<void> init() async {
    // Cancel existing subscriptions to prevent memory leak on app resume
    await _subscription?.cancel();
    await _connectivitySubscription?.cancel();
    _isDisposing = false;
    _isProcessing = false;

    _connectivitySubscription = _connectivity.onConnectivityChanged
        .debounceTime(connectivityDebounce)
        .listen(_onConnectivityChanged);

    _subscription = _outboxDao.watchUndelivered().listen(_onPendingEvents);
  }

  void _onConnectivityChanged(List<ConnectivityResult> results) {
    refresh();
  }

  @override
  Future<void> dispose() async {
    _isDisposing = true;

    // Wait for any in-flight operations to complete (with timeout)
    final timeout = DateTime.now().add(const Duration(seconds: 5));
    while (_isProcessing && DateTime.now().isBefore(timeout)) {
      await Future.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 50));
    }

    if (_isProcessing) {
      dev.log(
        'Warning: Disposed while still processing',
        name: 'OutboxPublisher',
      );
    }

    await _subscription?.cancel();
    _subscription = null;
    await _connectivitySubscription?.cancel();
    _connectivitySubscription = null;
    _retryTimer?.cancel();
    _retryTimer = null;
    dev.log('OutboxPublisher disposed', name: 'OutboxPublisher');
  }

  void refresh() {
    _isPaused = false;
    _subscription?.resume();
    _refreshRequested = true;
    _processQueue();
  }

  void pause() {
    _isPaused = true;
    _subscription?.pause();
    dev.log('OutboxPublisher paused', name: 'OutboxPublisher');
  }

  void resume() {
    _isPaused = false;
    _subscription?.resume();
    // Process any events that accumulated while paused
    _refreshRequested = true;
    _processQueue();
    dev.log('OutboxPublisher resumed', name: 'OutboxPublisher');
  }

  void _onPendingEvents(List<OutboxEventData> pending) {
    if (pending.isEmpty || _isPaused) return;
    if (_isProcessing) {
      _refreshRequested = true;
      return;
    }
    _refreshRequested = true;
    _processQueue();
  }

  Future<void> _processQueue() async {
    if (_isPaused || _isDisposing) return;
    if (_isProcessing) {
      _refreshRequested = true;
      return;
    }
    _isProcessing = true;

    try {
      do {
        _refreshRequested = false;
        final pending = await _outboxDao.getPending();

        for (final item in pending) {
          if (_isDisposing || _isPaused) break;

          try {
            await _publishEvent(item);
          } catch (e, stackTrace) {
            dev.log(
              'Exception processing ${item.eventId}: $e\n$stackTrace',
              name: 'OutboxPublisher',
              error: e,
              stackTrace: stackTrace,
            );
          }
        }
      } while (_refreshRequested && !_isPaused && !_isDisposing);
    } finally {
      _isProcessing = false;
    }
  }

  Future<void> _publishEvent(OutboxEventData item) async {
    try {
      final events = await _rawEventStore.queryEvents(
        RawEventQuery(ids: [item.eventId]),
      );

      if (events.isEmpty) {
        // The referenced event no longer exists; drop the orphaned entry.
        await _outboxDao.remove(item.eventId);
        dev.log(
          'Event ${item.eventId} not found in store, dropped from outbox',
          name: 'OutboxPublisher',
        );
        return;
      }

      final event = events.first;
      final relays = _relaysListRepo.getRelaysList();

      if (relays.isEmpty) {
        // Transient: no relays configured yet. Keep the entry and retry later.
        _scheduleRetry(item, 'No relays configured');
        return;
      }

      final client = NostrClient(channelFactory: _channelFactory);
      try {
        client.addRelays(relays);

        final publisher = NostrPublisher(client: client, event: event);
        final report = await publisher.execute();

        if (!report.isAnySuccess) {
          _scheduleRetry(item, report.error.toString());
        } else {
          // Delivered — remove from the outbox.
          await _outboxDao.remove(item.eventId);
          final confirmed = report.okEvents.where((e) => e.isOk).length;
          dev.log(
            'Published ${item.eventId} (${_getKindName(event.kind)}) '
            'to $confirmed relays',
            name: 'OutboxPublisher',
          );
        }
      } finally {
        await client.disconnectAndDispose();
      }
    } catch (e) {
      _scheduleRetry(item, e.toString());
      rethrow;
    }
  }

  /// Schedule a retry after a publish failure. The outbox row is left in place
  /// (a present row means "still needs delivery"), so no DB write happens here
  /// — that avoids re-triggering the watch stream and looping tightly. Fresh
  /// events retry sooner than old ones.
  void _scheduleRetry(OutboxEventData item, String reason) {
    dev.log(
      'Failed to publish ${item.eventId}: $reason',
      name: 'OutboxPublisher',
    );

    _retryTimer?.cancel();
    final ageMs = DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch - item.createdAt;
    final delay = ageMs < 5000 ? const Duration(seconds: 3) : _retryDelay;
    _retryTimer = Timer(delay, () {
      dev.log('Retrying outbox after $delay', name: 'OutboxPublisher');
      _processQueue();
    });
  }

  String _getKindName(int kind) {
    if (kind == EventKind.note.value) return 'note';
    if (kind == NostrKind.deletion) return 'deletion';
    return 'kind $kind';
  }
}

/// No-op implementation for testing
class NoopOutboxPublisher implements OutboxPublisher, Disposable {
  @override
  Future<void> init() async {}

  @override
  Future<void> dispose() async {}

  @override
  void refresh() {}

  @override
  void pause() {}

  @override
  void resume() {}

  @override
  StreamSubscription<List<ConnectivityResult>>? _connectivitySubscription;

  @override
  bool _isDisposing = false;

  @override
  bool _isPaused = false;

  @override
  bool _isProcessing = false;

  @override
  bool _refreshRequested = false;

  @override
  StreamSubscription<List<OutboxEventData>>? _subscription;

  @override
  ChannelFactory get _channelFactory => throw UnimplementedError();

  @override
  Connectivity get _connectivity => throw UnimplementedError();

  @override
  String _getKindName(int kind) {
    throw UnimplementedError();
  }

  @override
  void _scheduleRetry(OutboxEventData item, String reason) {}

  @override
  void _onConnectivityChanged(List<ConnectivityResult> results) {}

  @override
  void _onPendingEvents(List<OutboxEventData> pending) {}

  @override
  OutboxDaoInterface get _outboxDao => throw UnimplementedError();

  @override
  Future<void> _processQueue() async {}

  @override
  Future<void> _publishEvent(OutboxEventData item) async {}

  @override
  RawEventStore get _rawEventStore => throw UnimplementedError();

  @override
  RelaysListRepo get _relaysListRepo => throw UnimplementedError();

  @override
  Duration get connectivityDebounce => throw UnimplementedError();

  @override
  Timer? _retryTimer;
}

import 'package:common/services/event_store/database/app_database.dart';

/// Interface for OutboxDao to enable testing with mocks.
///
/// The outbox is a plain delivery queue: **a row exists iff the event still
/// needs to reach relays.** Successfully delivered events are removed.
abstract interface class OutboxDaoInterface {
  /// Queue an event for publishing.
  Future<void> insert({required String eventId});

  /// Get all events still awaiting delivery, oldest first.
  Future<List<OutboxEventData>> getPending();

  /// Watch events still awaiting delivery (drives the "not yet delivered" UI).
  Stream<List<OutboxEventData>> watchUndelivered();

  /// Remove a delivered event from the outbox.
  Future<void> remove(String eventId);

  /// Remove outbox entries by event IDs (e.g. when a note is replaced/deleted).
  Future<void> removeUndeliveredByEventIds(Set<String> eventIds);
}

import 'package:drift/drift.dart';
import 'package:common/services/event_store/database/app_database.dart';
import 'package:common/services/event_store/database/tables/outbox_events.dart';

import 'outbox_dao_interface.dart';

part 'outbox_dao.g.dart';

/// The outbox is a plain delivery queue: a row exists iff the event still needs
/// to reach relays. On success the row is removed.
///
/// The legacy `status` column is no longer written (rows stay at the default
/// `pending`); queries simply exclude any pre-existing `sent` rows from older
/// app versions so already-delivered events are not resurfaced.
@DriftAccessor(tables: [OutboxEvents])
class OutboxDao extends DatabaseAccessor<AppDatabase>
    with _$OutboxDaoMixin
    implements OutboxDaoInterface {
  OutboxDao(super.db);

  @override
  Future<void> insert({required String eventId}) async {
    await into(outboxEvents).insert(
      OutboxEventsCompanion.insert(
        eventId: eventId,
        createdAt: DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch,
      ),
      mode: InsertMode.insertOrIgnore,
    );
  }

  @override
  Future<List<OutboxEventData>> getPending() async {
    return (select(outboxEvents)
          ..where((o) => o.status.isNotValue(OutboxStatus.sent.index))
          ..orderBy([(o) => OrderingTerm.asc(o.createdAt)]))
        .get();
  }

  @override
  Stream<List<OutboxEventData>> watchUndelivered() {
    return (select(outboxEvents)
          ..where((o) => o.status.isNotValue(OutboxStatus.sent.index))
          ..orderBy([(o) => OrderingTerm.asc(o.createdAt)]))
        .watch();
  }

  @override
  Future<void> remove(String eventId) async {
    await (delete(outboxEvents)..where((o) => o.eventId.equals(eventId))).go();
  }

  @override
  Future<void> removeUndeliveredByEventIds(Set<String> eventIds) async {
    if (eventIds.isEmpty) return;
    await (delete(outboxEvents)..where(
          (o) =>
              o.eventId.isIn(eventIds) &
              o.status.isNotValue(OutboxStatus.sent.index),
        ))
        .go();
  }
}

/// Mock [ChannelFactory] returning [MockWSChannel] with configurable
/// auto-response behaviour for OK / fail.
class _MockChannelFactory implements ChannelFactory {
  bool respondWithOk = true;
  bool respondWithFail = false;

  final channels = <MockWSChannel>[];

  @override
  WsChannel create(String url) {
    final mock = MockWSChannel(url: url);

    if (respondWithOk || respondWithFail) {
      mock.onAdd = (data, channel) {
        if (data is! String) return;
        try {
          final decoded = jsonDecode(data) as List;
          if (decoded.isNotEmpty && decoded[0] == 'EVENT') {
            final event = decoded[1] as Map<String, dynamic>;
            final eventId = event['id'] as String;
            final ok = respondWithOk;
            final response = jsonEncode([
              'OK',
              eventId,
              ok,
              ok ? '' : 'test rejection',
            ]);
            channel.mockStream.add(response);
          }
        } catch (_) {}
      };
    }

    channels.add(mock);
    return mock;
  }
}

class _MockOutboxDao implements OutboxDaoInterface {
  bool watchUndeliveredCalled = false;
  List<String> removeCalledWith = [];

  final _pendingController = BehaviorSubject<List<OutboxEventData>>.seeded([]);

  @override
  Future<void> insert({required String eventId}) async {
    addPendingEvent(_createOutboxEvent(eventId));
  }

  void addPendingEvent(OutboxEventData event) {
    final current = List<OutboxEventData>.from(_pendingController.value);
    current.add(event);
    _pendingController.add(current);
  }

  @override
  Future<List<OutboxEventData>> getPending() async => _pendingController.value;

  @override
  Future<void> remove(String eventId) async {
    removeCalledWith.add(eventId);
    final current = List<OutboxEventData>.from(_pendingController.value);
    current.removeWhere((e) => e.eventId == eventId);
    _pendingController.add(current);
  }

  @override
  Future<void> removeUndeliveredByEventIds(Set<String> eventIds) async {
    final current = List<OutboxEventData>.from(_pendingController.value);
    current.removeWhere((e) => eventIds.contains(e.eventId));
    _pendingController.add(current);
  }

  @override
  Stream<List<OutboxEventData>> watchUndelivered() {
    watchUndeliveredCalled = true;
    return _pendingController.stream;
  }

  void dispose() {
    _pendingController.close();
  }
}

class _MockConnectivity implements Connectivity {
  final _controller = StreamController<List<ConnectivityResult>>.broadcast();
  List<ConnectivityResult> _currentResult = [ConnectivityResult.wifi];

  void setConnectivity(List<ConnectivityResult> results) {
    _currentResult = results;
    _controller.add(results);
  }

  @override
  Future<List<ConnectivityResult>> checkConnectivity() async => _currentResult;

  @override
  Stream<List<ConnectivityResult>> get onConnectivityChanged =>
      _controller.stream;
}

## Что сделано

Outbox схлопнут до модели **«строка есть ⇒ событие ещё не доставлено»** (без миграции, колонки физически остались, но в коде больше не используются).

**Поведение публикации** ([outbox_publisher.dart](packages/notes/lib/services/outbox_publisher.dart)):
- success → `remove(eventId)` (удаляем строку) вместо `markSent`+статус `sent`;
- failure → **ничего не пишем в БД**, просто планируем ретрай таймером (свежие — через 3с, старые — 20с). Нет записи → нет лишней эмиссии `watchUndelivered` → нет тайт-лупа;
- event не найден в store → удаляем осиротевшую строку;
- конкурентность держит только in-memory `_isProcessing`.

**DAO** ([outbox_dao.dart](packages/common/lib/services/event_store/database/daos/outbox_dao.dart), [интерфейс](packages/common/lib/services/event_store/database/daos/outbox_dao_interface.dart)) — с 12 методов до 5: `insert`, `getPending`, `watchUndelivered`, `remove`, `removeUndeliveredByEventIds`. Запросы фильтруют `status != sent` — чисто ради обратной совместимости со старыми БД (не воскрешать уже доставленные).

**Удалено как мёртвое:** `broadcasting`/`markBroadcasting`, `markSent`/`confirmedRelays`, `markFailed`/`failed`/`failureReason`, `retryFailed`/`retryAllFailed`, `getFailed`, `cleanupOldSent`/`cleanup`, `attemptCount`-логика, `deleteSent`, `watchPending`, а также мой временный `resetStaleBroadcasting`.

**Чем это лучше:**
1. Твой баг с «Bugs» чинится **в корне** — нет состояния `broadcasting`, в котором можно застрять. Старые orphan-строки (`broadcasting`/`failed`) теперь сами подхватываются `getPending` и переотправляются.
2. Уходит вечная утечка `sent`-строк (cleanup в проде и так не вызывался).
3. Тайт-луп ретраев устранён конструктивно, а не таймерным костылём.

**Тесты:** 15 в outbox-сьюте + 13 в notes-юзкейсах зелёные. Добавлен явный тест на back-compat фильтр `legacy sent rows`.

Колонки в таблице можно будет дропнуть отдельной миграцией (v2→v3), когда захочешь — это уже чистая косметика схемы.

31	  /// The next biometry check will be skipped and the user will be allowed back
32	  /// without being sent to the PIN screen.
33	  void skipNextVerification() {
34	    _skipNextVerification = true;
35	  }
36	
37	  VerificationUsecase({
38	    required this.biometricRepository,
39	    required this.appLifecycleListenerRepository,
40	    required AuthUsecase authUsecase,
41	    this.maxInactiveDuration = defaultMaxInactiveDuration,
42	    this.debounceGuard = defaultDebounceGuard,
43	  }) : _authUsecase = authUsecase;
44	
45	  Stream<Verification> createStream({
46	    required BiometricRepositoryRequest biometryRequest,
47	  }) {
48	    return appLifecycleListenerRepository.isActiveStream
49	        .distinct()
50	        .switchMap(
51	          (isActive) => _skipNextVerification
52	              ? Stream.value(isActive)
53	              : TimerStream(isActive, debounceGuard),
54	        )
55	        .asyncExpand((isActive) {
56	          _isActive = isActive;
57	          if (!isActive) {
58	            setDeniedAtIfNeeded();
59	            // Controlled background (e.g. ad) — skip blur entirely.
60	            // Return directly to bypass the .map(_isActive check) below.
61	            if (_skipNextVerification) {
62	              return Stream.value(const Verification.allow());
63	            }
64	          }
65	
66	          final isLocked = !_authUsecase.currentSession.isUnlocked;
67	
68	          if (isLocked) {
69	            return Stream.value(const Verification.allow());
70	          }
71	
72	          return _performAuthorizationIfNeeded(
73	            isActive: isActive,
74	            biometryRequest: biometryRequest,
75	          ).map((value) {
76	            final isLocked = !_authUsecase.currentSession.isUnlocked;
77	            // In unauthorized zone blur must never be shown.
78	            if (isLocked) {
79	              return const Verification.allow();
80	            }
81	            // Preserve explicit Deny from biometry failure — the lock overlay
82	            // must stay visible while the session is still authorized.
83	            if (value == const Verification.deny()) {
84	              return const Verification.deny();
85	            }
86	            return _isActive ? value : const Verification.deny();
87	          });
88	        })
89	        .doOnData((e) {
90	          log(
91	            'Result verification status ${e.toString()}',
92	            name: 'VerificationUsecase',
93	          );
94	        })
95	        .distinct();
96	  }
97	
98	  Stream<Verification> _performAuthorizationIfNeeded({
99	    required bool isActive,
100	    required BiometricRepositoryRequest biometryRequest,
101	  }) async* {
102	    final denyTime = _deniedAt;
103	
104	    if (isActive && denyTime != null) {
105	      final skip = _skipNextVerification;
106	      _skipNextVerification = false;
107	      if (skip || !_isOutdated(denyTime: denyTime)) {
108	        resetDenyTime();
109	        yield const Verification.allow();
110	      } else {
111	        yield const Verification.processing();
112	        final status = await _passBiometry(biometricRequest: biometryRequest);
113	        yield status;
114	      }
115	    } else {
116	      yield const Verification.deny();
117	    }
118	  }
119	
120	  bool _isOutdated({required DateTime denyTime}) {
121	    return denyTime.add(maxInactiveDuration).isBefore(DateTime.now());
122	  }
123	
124	  Future<Verification> _passBiometry({
125	    required BiometricRepositoryRequest biometricRequest,
126	  }) async {
127	    try {
128	      final isAuthorized = await biometricRepository.execute(biometricRequest);
129	
130	      if (isAuthorized) {
131	        resetDenyTime();
132	        return const Verification.allow();
133	      } else {
134	        await _authUsecase.restore();
135	        resetDenyTime();
136	        return const Verification.deny();
137	      }
138	    } catch (e) {
139	      await _authUsecase.restore();
140	      return const Verification.deny();
141	    }
142	  }
143	
144	  @override
145	  Future<void> dispose() async {}
146	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-14 19:56:08Z)**_

Прочитал всю цепочку. Теперь могу точно диагностировать оба бага — и они security-чувствительные, поэтому перед правкой подтвержу намерение.

## Диагноз

**Баг 1 — блюр возвращается поверх активного приложения.**
В [createStream](packages/notes/lib/common/domain/usecase/verification_usecase.dart#L45) стоит `switchMap` (на lifecycle) + `asyncExpand` (на верификацию). У `asyncExpand` семантика concatMap — он **не отменяет** предыдущий inner, а ставит следующие в очередь. Системный диалог FaceID сам переводит приложение в `inactive`(false). Пока внутри `asyncExpand` идёт `await _passBiometry`, это `false` копится в очереди. После успеха биометрии (`Allow`) `asyncExpand` обрабатывает устаревший `false` → `_performAuthorizationIfNeeded(isActive:false)` → ветка `!isActive` → **`Deny`**. Отсюда лог `Processing → inactive:false → Allow → resumed:true → Deny`.

**Баг 2 — обход FaceID быстрым фон→возврат.**
Окно грации `maxInactiveDuration = 35с`: при возврате, если `now - denyTime < 35с`, пускает **без** биометрии ([:107](packages/notes/lib/common/domain/usecase/verification_usecase.dart#L107)). После долгого фона требуется FaceID, но вместо него можно кратко свернуть/развернуть — и грация снимает блюр без биометрии. `denyTime` сбрасывается в null в т.ч. при неудачной биометрии ([:135](packages/notes/lib/common/domain/usecase/verification_usecase.dart#L135)), что усугубляет.

Баг 1 — однозначно баг, чиню в любом случае. Баг 2 упирается в продуктовое решение про грацию — это и спрошу.

**Как должно работать окно грации (35с) при возврате из фона в Unlocked-сессии?**

Options:
- **Грация до первого требования FaceID** - Если ушёл <35с — пускать без биометрии (удобство). Но как только FaceID потребовался (ушёл >35с) — залатчить: любой последующий быстрый фон→возврат всё равно требует FaceID, пока он реально не пройдён. Закрывает обход, сохраняет удобство.
- **Всегда требовать FaceID** - Убрать грацию полностью: любой возврат из фона в Unlocked-сессии требует биометрии. Максимальная строгость, но FaceID на каждый возврат (даже после короткого взгляда в сторону).
- **Только починить баг 1** - Грацию не трогать (обход остаётся), починить только лишний Deny поверх активного приложения. Если обход некритичен или решается отдельно.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-14 20:06:10Z)**_

All 15 pass, including the new blip test. Both bugs fixed.

## Итог

Оба бага были в [verification_usecase.dart](packages/notes/lib/common/domain/usecase/verification_usecase.dart). (Они проявились только сейчас, потому что раньше файл не компилировался из-за кривого импорта `dart:developer` — приложение крутило старую сборку.)

**Баг 1 — блюр возвращался поверх активного приложения.**
Системный диалог FaceID сам переводит приложение в `inactive`, а `asyncExpand` (concatMap, не отменяет) ставил это `inactive` в очередь за `await` биометрии и обрабатывал уже после `Allow` → лишний `Deny`.
Фикс: флаг `_isVerifying` + `.where((_) => !_isVerifying)` в начале стрима — lifecycle-блипы, вызванные самим промптом, отфильтровываются в реальном времени.

**Баг 2 — обход FaceID быстрым фон→возврат.**
Грация 35с + сброс `denyTime` при неудачной биометрии позволяли проскочить без аутентификации.
Фикс (по выбранной семантике «грация до первого требования FaceID»): латч `_reauthRequired` — взводится, как только биометрия становится нужна (вышли >35с), и снимается **только** при реальном успехе FaceID. Пока латч взведён, грация не применяется. На неудаче `denyTime` больше не сбрасывается. При locked-сессии латч и `denyTime` сбрасываются (после PIN-разблокировки — чистый старт, грация снова доступна).

Заодно `_evaluate` стал линейным и читаемым вместо вложенного `_performAuthorizationIfNeeded` + `.map`.

**Тесты:** 15 зелёных, включая новый детерминированный тест на блипы промпта (через `Completer`, удерживающий биометрию «в процессе»).

Хочешь — добавлю отдельный тест на латч (что после требования FaceID быстрый фон→возврат всё равно зовёт биометрию), но это потребует мока с задержкой; ключевой фикс уже покрыт.
